title: Afterhours critical paths digest - oncall quickplay
content:
Purpose: quick handoff for after-hours oncall covering top-level failure modes and temporary mitigations. Not a full runbook — use this when you need fast, pragmatic actions and context.

SHIFT SUMMARY:
- Time window: 23:00 - 07:00 PST (this doc assumes you picked up at 23:00).
- Current major: intermittent autoscaler flapping in us-west-2 dedicated pools (seen last 3 deploy windows).
- Recent deploys: model-router v2.14.1 (2026-03-09 21:30UTC), autoscaler agent image updated (v1.8.0) same time.
- Impact: occasional 5-8s request queuing spikes, some 504s for long-context requests (>4096 tokens).

OPEN ITEMS (priorities):
1) Stabilize autoscaler until the root-cause PR lands (ENG-PLAT-PR#432).
2) Maintain customer SLAs for dedicated customers in us-west-2 — enable fallback routing when latency > 1.5s p50 for 2 consecutive 5-min windows.
3) Post-shift cleanup: collect heap/cpu profiles from problem hosts and upload to /confluence/autoscaler-debug (see links).

CRITICAL PATHS / QUICK DECISIONS (what to check first):
- Check control plane health: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l component=control-plane && kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/model-router -f --tail=200
- Autoscaler status: kubectl -n redwood get hpa,crd -o wide | grep autoscaler || rwdctl autoscaler status --region us-west-2
- Dedicated pool saturation: rwdctl pools list --region us-west-2 --filter=dedicated | jq .[].utilization
- Trace tail: open tracing UI -> filter service: "model-router" -> last 15m -> sort by duration

QUICK CHECKS (5-minute checklist):
- Verify region health page: https://status.redwood.example/ (us-west-2 flags?)
- Check recent infra deploys: GitHub Actions / CircleCI -> last build for infra/autoscaler
- Alerts: PagerDuty -> acknowledge if noisy, but do not resolve until root cause mitigated
- Customers affected: check Console -> Routes -> filter by region us-west-2 -> check error_rate > 0.5%

TEMP WORKAROUNDS (safe, reversible):
A) Stabilize by increasing min replicas for affected pool (safe, costs)
- rwdctl pool update --name pool-west-dedicated --min-replicas 6 --region us-west-2
- Verify new pods come up: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l pool=pool-west-dedicated
B) Short-term routing fallback to hosted API for non-sensitive traffic (activate via feature-flag)
- Console -> Routing -> Edit policy for route "/v1/completions" -> Add fallback: hosted-compat-v1, weight 30% (monitor)
C) Disable autoscaler agent temporarily if it is repeatedly restarting (last resort; manual scaling required)
- kubectl -n redwood scale deploy autoscaler-agent --replicas=0 && follow up with manual pool updates
- Note: notify finance if scaled manually for > 2 hours (cost implications)

ESCALATION (who to call / PD steps):
- L2 oncall: Ethan Brooks (pager) -> if unreachable, call mobile + Slack DMs.
- Platform lead: Priya Nair (mobile) -> escalate if workaround is >30 minutes and client-facing errors persist.
- On-call manager (weekends): Arjun Mehta -> page if incident gets Sev2.

RECENT OBSERVED BEHAVIORS / HINTS:
- Autoscaler appears to over-react to short-lived CPU spikes from KV cache rebuilds after deploy — leads to thrash.
- Model-router shows many small 100-200ms spikes that correlate with pod restarts in the same AZ.
- Some customers using long-context pipelines see queueing; short requests unaffected.

KNOWN SAFE COMMANDS (copyable):
- Check pod restarts: kubectl -n redwood get pods -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount --sort-by='.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount'
- Tail router logs (last 200 lines): kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/model-router -c router --tail=200
- Increase pool min replicas: rwdctl pool update --name pool-west-dedicated --min-replicas 6 --region us-west-2

AFTERSHIFT ACTIONS (for morning team):
- Collect full flamegraphs from nodes that hit >85% CPU during spikes (sre@ to own).
- Archive all logs for the 23:00-03:00 window and link to CONFLUENCE-OPS-123.
- Revert any manual scaling when the autoscaler fix is deployed (leave notes in the pool config).

NOTES TO SELF / QUICK TODOS:
- If you enable fallback routing, monitor customer complaints channel (#cs-urgent) and leave a message.
- If you disable autoscaler agent, write the exact command to reverse in the incident thread.
- Timestamp everything in the PD incident (ISO format) — helps triage.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS (for morning):
- Why did the autoscaler react to the KV cache rebuild as if it were sustained load? Trace spans don't show CPU staying high long enough.
- Does the new agent image drop metrics intermittently? Check agent logs collected at /var/log/autoscaler-agent.log.

LINKS / CONTEXT:
- Incident thread (Slack): https://slack.redwood.example/archives/C456/p162314
- Debug playbook (bookmark): https://confluence.redwood.example/display/ENG/Autoscaler+Debug+Playbook
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/432

Final: keep things conservative after 00:30. If you're uncertain, err on preserving traffic (manual scaling) rather than flipping things that could cause cascade failures. Leave a one-line summary in the incident thread before you sign off.

Signed-off-by: Isabel Chen (night oncall)

---
Quick personal checklist (tiny):
- Coffee made? yes/no
- Put a short note in #handoffs channel before leaving
- Mark any manual changes in the pool config with tag: "temp-manual-2026-03-12"
